items.summary: News from two former members: Bill Spenser, now cycle racing at 70, and Bernard Eglinton, ex-RAF walker writing from Colwyn Bay.
items.text:
BILL SPENSER - Ex Met. Police now retired and living near Bury St. Edmunds was one of our Road Running stalwarts, but writes to say that he got a bit tired of walking around the country lanes so decided to get on his bike. So after a lapse of 50 years and at the age of 70 he has resumed Road Time-Trials Cycle Racing and intends to keep it up until - as he puts it - to the end of the chapter. Last October he cycled to Newmarket to see Stan Davies and sends regards to all and in particular Frank Webb, Norman Dewberry and Arthur Penstone,

BERNARD EGLINTON - Ex R.A.F. regular who joined the club as a runner from Derby AC and eventually excelled as a walker and scored in a number of National 50kms and 20mls R.W.A. Championship teams wins for the Bels, writes from his home in Colwyn Bay, Clwyd, N.Wales with Welsh flavoured fervour and sends greetings to all.

items.heading: WELCOME TO MATTHEW STICKLES
items.summary: Profile welcoming junior middle-distance runner Matthew Stickles to Belgrave, with his record and personal bests.
items.text:
With fine performances in the Surrey League and Junior Southern C.C. Championship Matthew Stickles has shown what a fine addition he is to Belgrave's middle distance ranks.

Born in February 1969, Matthew is still a junior in the Country in the UK, but is too old now to compeete as an International under the different International age groupings. He started running at the age of 12 and has performed with distinction at all age groups. In 1987 he was 3rd in the Junior AAA's 3000m in a p.b. of 8.18 and gained his first GB Junior vest as a result when he ran 8.20 in a W.Germany & Swiss triangular match. He came third in the '88 Junior later. Counties and his track p.b's include 800 - 1.53.7 and 1500 - 3.51.2. He has never run a 5000m although under Coach Steve Gosling's guidance this will be remedied in 1989. Certainly Matthew has wintered well, including a strengthening programme under the aegis of Mike Winch at the Belgrave Gym. We look forward with anticipation to Matthew's summer performances.

items.heading: NORFOLK WELCOMES BELGRAVE AND BELGRAVE WELCOMES NORFOLK
items.summary: Bill Laws's profiles of the Norfolk internationals who joined Belgrave in 1988: Paul Evans, Neil Fetherby, Darren Mead and Ian Wells.
items.text:
Five years ago we had a Cup Match in Norwich and past President, Tom Morrell and his family, who had moved to the area many years earlier, backed up our travelling supporters. At that time a few of us could have anticipated that in 1988 several of Norfolk's top runners would chose Belgrave as their club. Bill Laws has talked to our latest batch of Internationals who you will be seeing in action in the near future.

PAUL EVANS - Age 27:

Paul Evans started running to get fit for football which he played for Lowestoft. His training involved 2 days per week and it was with some reluctance that he entered his first road race - a Carnival 10km in August 1986. To everyones surprise he finished 7th in 33.33. A month later he ran 32.30 and was hooked. Hugh Elder took over as coach and within 6 months Paul had run two ½ marathons, the second one in 65.30. In August '87 he gained his first England vest when he ran in a Home Counties ½ marathon in Scotland. He finished a very creditable 6th reducing his p.b. to 64.31. In 1988 he ran his first 3000m and became the first Brit. to run a sub 8.00 in a debut race. Since then he has represented the ECCU in several overseas races. His track p.b's (as of February 1989) are: 1 mile - 4.02, 3000m - 7.57, 2 miles - 8.32.2, 5000m - 13.57, 10,000m - 29.08.

NEIL FETHERBY - Age (stopped counting at 27)

Neil Fetherby is a true ultra-distance runner who thrives on the 120+ miles/week training schedules imposed by coach Bud Bolders. His International career started in 1986 when he represented England in the Aberdeen Marathon. He ran the Berlin Marathon twice and on the second occasion set a p.b. of 2.17.35. He gained a full GB vest in the 87 Koscite Marathon following wins in the Wolverhampton and Norfolk Marathons. Since joining Belgrave in 1988 he has been dogged by injury and only now is getting back to past form. His 10KM is 30.20.

DARREN MEAD - Age 20 years

Darren Mead is a legend in his own young life time. Twice winner of the Youths National C.C. Championship he gained his first England vest in the 1986 Junior World Championships where he finished 12th. He gained a GB vest in 1986 where he ran the World Junior and ran 14.12.3 for 5000m at the age of 17. 1987 saw a period of re-trenchment and it was not until 1988 that Darren started to re-gain form. He finished 2nd in the National Junior C.C. Championships and following a move to Sutton joined Belgrave and immediately made our British League Team running 800, 1500 and 5000m. His current p.b's confirm a surprising turn of speed which could well prove his most valuable weapon in the years ahead. At present he is self-coached and self-employed in the carpet business.
P.b's: 200m: 23.7, 400m: 50.5, 800m: 1.52.6, 1500m: 3.45.8, 3000m: 8.08.0, 5000m: 14.12.3, 10,000m: 29.20, 10 Miles 49.03.

IAN WELLS - Age 26

Ian Wells has been the Civil Service 400mH champion for the last 4 years. He has joined Belgrave to increase his opportunities for top class competition which is limited in the Great Yarmouth area. His choice of Belgrave was as a result of meeting fellow Civil Service athletes Abi Ekoku, Jay Busk and Derrick Williams. He aims to train at Battersea Park with Bob Bridges squad at least once per month. His p.b's are: 110H: 15.5, 400H: 54.72, 400m: 50.6 and Decathlon 4602 pts.

items.heading: Leo Coy, President 1989.
items.summary: Bill Laws's tribute to new club president Leo Coy, tracing his running career and his work rebuilding Belgrave's track and field team.
items.text:
The election in September 1988 of Leo Coy as President gave particular pleasure to those who know how much work he has put into reviving Belgrave's Track and Field fortunes.

Like so many of our officials Leo's arrival at Belgrave and involvement in the management side was as a result of a series of coincidences. He started running seriously in 1968 following encouragement from TVH's International 800m man Peter Browne. He so easily could have joined TVH. But no, he 'phoned the AAA's who thought he might consider Belgrave, met Alf Harley at Battersea and in 1969 was in!

Belgravian reports of the time spotted this 'new talent' and he was soon making teams which included past greats like Gerry North, Bill Curtin, and Peter Carton. He ran in two 6 stage National road relay teams and five Southern 12 stage road relay teams. Somewhat later he won the Club 3000m s/c Champs.

But already other interests were encroaching. In Charlie Manning's Presidential Year - the 'infamous '74' - Leo was cajoled to organise a fund raising fashion show and did so with great success. In '75 he became an official NUT and since then has been responsible for compiling the UK Top 100 performances in the steeplechase 5000 and 10,000m. In '77 he was elected assistant Hon. Gen. Sec. first to Peter Hillier and then Ray Hall.

In 1980 when our 'A' team T&F side were struggling at the bottom of Southern League Div.1 Leo decided something had to be done and embarked on a team rebuilding exercise which virtually put paid to his own serious training plans. The success of his efforts could be seen as Belgrave moved from 35th in the National Rankings to its current 3rd place in Div.1 of the British Athletics League. 8 years of solid hard work. Add to that 4 years as Young Athletes Secretary and his current job as Coaching Secretary and you will appreciate just how much Leo has done for Belgrave.

During all this he has been ably and loyally supported by his family who on many occasions have been seen together at T&F matches looking after entries, recording, scoring and the myriad of jobs needed to ensure successful organisation. While wife Sue and daughter Nemone are strictly back-room helpers, son Jon has run for Belgrave over many years and is a rapidly improving Junior.

So well done Leo, you thoroughly deserve the Honour.

Bill Laws

people.name: Leo Coy
people.note: elected President September 1988; joined 1969; won Club 3000m s/c championship; NUT statistician; assistant Hon. Gen. Sec. from 1977; rebuilt T&F team from 1980; Young Athletes Secretary and Coaching Secretary

items.heading: W.E.LUCAS D.F.C.
items.summary: Charlie Manning's tribute to Bill Lucas, Belgrave's centenary-year president.
items.text:
I do not think we should let Memory of our Centenary Year fade too far from our minds without remembering our 'Centenary' President.

We were singularly lucky in having a man of that calibre to front our Club. There are many opinions of Bill - not all see him as sweetness and light (I'm one myself) - some think him high handed (yea' I'll go along with that too) most of us have felt the rough edge of his tongue, he doesn't suffer fools gladly and gives short shrift to incompetance idleness and excuses.

Hell of a downside isn't there! But the Past Presidents and Committee and Officers put him forward confident that he could serve us. This he has done with distinction.

Bill is one of those rare people who are gifted with an abundance of qualities - I won't mention his 1948 Olympic selection - or his war record - or his announcing at International meets - or even his position on the 3 A's Executive Committee.

What I will say is "Thank you Bill, you've been a great President during an historic period of our Club - your energy - your dedication - your loyalty to Belgrave Harriers, your personal standing in the broad spectrum of athletics - your impartial enthusiasm for every aspect of our activities - is a tribute to yourself, a benefit to the Club and an inspiration to us all.

Thank you.

CHARLIE MANNING

items.heading: From the President.
items.summary: New president Leo Coy's message on Belgrave Hall, the need for new members, committee volunteers and a Young Athletes organiser.
items.text:
Thank you for electing me President of this great Club. I am deeply honoured to undertake this role for this great Club. The position of President in the Club is unique in that you are not given a description of what you should be doing, you are elected and left to get on with it. There are a number of things that I would like your help to achieve, that will be enjoyable for you and very beneficial to the Club.

Belgrave Hall
One of my aims as President will be to increase the use of Belgrave Hall by Club Members. The Hall is being given a much needed facelift, thanks to the efforts of Tom Carter. Mike Winch is basing all his activities under one roof at Belgrave Hall and this will give us a boost in income and make it a unique Centre of Excellence.
A spin-off from this is that the Hall will be open for training on seven days a week. So, get up to the Hall as often as possible, get out for a run, and have a cup of tea or a pint afterwards.

New Members
For a Club with a membership of over 600 you may be surprised to learn that we desperately need new members, of all ages, particularly young athletes, male and female. All new members should be encouraged to train from Belgrave Hall or from Battersea Park Track and this in turn will develop a foundation for the Club to progress in the future.

Belgrave Committee
The organisation of Belgrave is placed by you in the hands of the Committee which is elected each year at the AGM. There are about six people who sit on this Committee, that virtually run Belgrave with very little input or ideas from the Club Membership. Should one of these stalwarts decide that they have had enough and cease their activities, then the club would be in real difficulties. We need new administrators, new ideas and more Club Members involved in running Belgrave. If you can spare an hour a week please let me or a Committee Member know. Any help however small would be much appreciated.

Young Athletes
At one time we had a regular influx of youngsters to fill our teams. This influx has dried up and we now have very few young athletes, girls or boys. We have also got nobody to organise the Young Athletes, which is an unbelievable situation for a Club as distinguished as ours. It is for you to decide whether we continue with running a Young Athletes Section, if nobody comes forward in the very near future then we will have no alternative but to restrict the age of our new members. Please help us to avoid this happening.

Thank you for your time and your support so far in my year of office. Remember that no club can survive for long if everybody just turns up for a race or a training run. We need your help now to form a solid foundation for this our second century.

We have a great deal going for us at present, the performances of our Junior Cross-Country Teams throughout the eighties is the envy of most other clubs in the country, our Track and Field Team is our best ever. Have you been to support our Juniors or Track and Field side? You don't know what you are missing.

Good luck throughout 1989.

LEO COY
President

items.heading: From THE BELGRAVIAN 25 years ago.... and 40 years ago.
items.summary: Look-back column quoting the Belgravian of April 1967 (headed '25 years ago', as printed) on E.C.C.U. championship results and SCAAA committee elections, and of June 1949 on Percy Wright's Overseas Trophy appeal.
items.text:
From THE BELGRAVIAN

25 years ago....

"April 1967 - our combined record in Youths, Juniors and Senior E.C.C.U. Championships this year was second only to one other Club - Coventry Godiva H. We were 12th in the Youths race (of 120 Clubs); 9th in the Junior (of 105 Clubs) and 8th in the Senior (of 135 Clubs) - a really splendid combined effort in which we can take great pride. In addition, our congratulations go to Gerry North on his sixth place in the Senior and on International selection; to Tony Fairclough - 5th in the Junior Championship; and to John Bicourt, seventh in the Youths event. All this magnificent running in fields of fantastic size, and its promise for the future.

In the recent ballot for the Committee of the Southern Counties Amateur Athletic Association our General Hon. Sec. Alf Harley was placed equal third in the voting, Les Cohen was 5th and Harry Shields equal 14th of the twenty elected members. Bill Lucas, our President, represents the Southern Cross-Country Association and Frank Jarvis the Race Walking Association, Southern Area."

and 40 years ago.

"June 1949 - THE OVERSEAS TROPHY - Percy Wright says:- 'Remember it? We planned it for after the war with the money that we made on those Airgraphs you chaps sent me. Unfortunately the man that bought the Airgraphs died and this source of income died with him. We had, however, succeeded in getting quite a tidy sum - £6. 19s. 6d., to be exact. I had hoped to plan something else to raise the money to a sufficient sum to purchase a suitable trophy, but my present distance from the Club quarters is not convenient. It has been suggested to me that I make an appeal to all those who served overseas and would like to see the idea of the Overseas Cup materialise to send along a subscription. Well, lads! what about it? Send your cheque, postal order or stamp, either to me or the Hon. Treasurer, not forgetting to mention what it is for. We should also be pleased to have any suggestions on how the trophy shall be awarded.' "

(The "Overseas Cup" was designated the Championship Trophy for the Youth cross-country event.)

items.heading: IN MEMORIUM: R.M. 'MEL' THORPE (Born March 1938 - died November 1988)
items.summary: Clive Shippen's obituary of Mel Thorpe, a Belgrave distance runner of the 1960s who came from and returned to Coventry Godiva.
items.text:
IN MEMORIUM

R.M. 'MEL' THORPE
(Born March 1938 - died November 1988)

It is with sadness that we must report the death of Mel Thorpe. Mel was an integral part of the Belgrave running teams of the 1960's and, with his wife Mary, ever present at the numerous social functions the team enjoyed in those days.

When he knew he would be moving South from Coventry Godiva Harriers he joined Belgrave and was elected to membership in August 1963. By the time he had got himself settled in it was March 1964 and his first appearance for us was at the Bexley Relay where he was put in the 'C' team as a 'feeler'. His performance proved to the selectors that he was a serious candidate for our 1st team and he confirmed that view in his first season with us.

His enthusiasm for running carried him across a wide spectrum of distances, from one mile on the track to 20 miles on the road, all in that first season with us which culminated in Mel helping the Bels to a fine second place in the News of the World "Southern" London to Brighton Relay.

From then on he was ubiquitous, cramming in to four seasons what many would take double that time to achieve. Hardly a team was fielded without his presence. His best performances on the track were 4:19.8 for the mile, 9:04 for two miles and 14:13 for three miles. In the "5 3/4" he ran 28:34 and in the Yacht '3' the second fastest time ever of 14:37, only Gerry North having run faster.

But after 4 years of wearing Belgrave colours over track, country and road - and giving us sterling support in all our affairs - his job took him back to Coventry. He retained second-claim membership of Bels for very many years and he and Mary always looked forward to their re-union visits South.

The Belgravian of March 1967 wrote:-

"We suppose it was inevitable. To hope to hang on to Mel Thorpe indefinitely when he now lives in distant Coventry was too good to be true ..... he will now probably run against us in the National Road Relay wearing the colours of Godiva. Mel writes 'I thank all those at Belgrave for the happiest four years of my life'. It was a pleasure to have you Mel".

Our condolences are extended to Mary, Karen and Richard.

CLIVE SHIPPEN

items.heading: L.A.MITCHELL (LEN)
items.summary: Obituary of race-walking official Len Mitchell, former R.W.A. President, who died on 9 January 1989 aged 82.
items.text:
L.A.MITCHELL (LEN) - passed away January 9th, 1989 aged 82. Len became a member of Belgrave only in the last couple of years, but had been a good friend of the club for many years. He had served the Race-Walking sport at all levels, both as a competitor and official. He had been President of the R.W.A. National and also Southern Area and had also held secretarial positions in the R.W.A. and Surrey County AAA.

He moved to Trowbridge on 14 December, 1988 after a lifetime in the Croydon area only to survive a matter of weeks. He was cremated at Bath on January 18th and a number of club members attended.

We extend our sincere condolences to Mrs. B. Mitchell and family.

items.summary: Club gossip column: Eddie Kulukundis's OBE and Athletics Today, news of former members, the Southern Cross-Country team, officials' elections (Cyril Gittens, Doug Fotheringham), engagements, marriages, Dave Davies's police trophy and members' operations.
items.text:
Our congratulations go out to our Patron, EDDIE KULUKUNDIS, on his OBE in the New Year Honours List. The award, for his services as Chairman of the Sports Aid Foundation and to Athletics, was highly deserved. His deep knowledge of athletics and his enthusiasm for helping promising youngsters is well known. Many established internationals have benefitted from his past help and many future teams will spring from his present support. We feel sure that his association with athletics will be long and fruitful.

************

DAYE DONOVAN writes from New York and reciprocates our wishes for a Happy New Year. She recently enjoyed an intoxicating trip around India, but did not see Rangit Bhatia in her travels. She hopes to be in England again in May and looks forward to seeing us again.

************

RANJIT BHATIA, professor of mathematics at Delhi University, sends best wishes to all his former club-mates at Belgrave. Rangit writes and broadcasts on athletics and was in Seoul for the Olympics, where he met Eddie Kulukundis and cheered on John Regis with full Belgrave partiality. His knowledge of athletics won him an Addidas forecast prize and a round-the-world trip. He still carries his Belgrave vest over the roads of India.

************

How good it was to see three Belgrave vests up in the first eight of the Southern Cross-Country Championships at Basingstoke. Matthew Stickles, Darren Mead and Justin Chaston ran superbly and are certain to pull each other through to many successes in the future. Steve Webster carried a heavy burden as 4th scorer in such a team, but he performed with great credit to clinch second place for Belgrave, only 4 points behind the winners.

************

CLIVE SHIPPEN was elected a vice-President of the Southern Counties AA in 1988. Bill Lucas (now 72) continues to shoulder the burden of Chairman during a period of much change and controversy at Area and National level.

************

EDDIE KULUKUNDIS is the new publisher of ATHLETICS TODAY. The magazine is now appearing weekly and is produced by a formidable team of journalists and athletes. It is probably the best magazine on athletics to ever hit the British market. We wish Eddie and his team every success in their enterprise.

Race Walking Association - National President 1989.

Congratulations to Cyril Gittens on his election to this top post. Cyril has been a second claim member for 36 years and other than a competitor has given yeoman service to the club as an official and in particular as time keeper.

1989 should be an exciting year for Ernest Obeng. He has recently started a Sport Promotions Business which offers, among other things, a low cost electronic timing system for track meets. And in May he marries Sharon whom he met as a post graduate student at Loughborough University. Sharon gained her Doctorate last summer.

Marriage next too for fellow sprint star Lenny Paul who we understand is planning 'To tie the knot' before the '89 track season.

Not to be left behind middle distance junior star, Darren Mead has recently announced his engagement to Donna. Just to show what a small world it is, Donna who lives in Norfolk, is the niece of former Surrey C.C.Champ. John Roberts.

You may have read in the press of John Gladwin's M.E. illness. In a final attempt to free himself of the debilitating after effects, John is to spend 5 months 5 months in Australia at the same Canberra Sports Institute that initiated the remarkable breakthrough of Gary Staines in 1987. In both cases the trips were financed by our patron Eddie Kulukundis.

Congratulations to John and Jane Barry who are expecting their first child in May.

JOINT SECRETARIES

Club Officials are liable to get 'phone calls at all hours and awkward times and our Gen.Hon.Sec., Sue Morrison is no exception.

Christmas Day Dinnertime made no difference when she literally received a ring from The Ladies Section Hon. Sec., Harry Porter. Having popped the proposal between courses and they are happy to announce their engagement. Congratulations to Sue and Harry!!

Dave Davies Perpetuated (Not a painful operation)

On September 6th, 1988 at a function following a Kent Police and City of London Police 10 Miles Road Running Championships Race, the following report appeared in The City Police Magazine "City '88" - New Trophy - The presentation Buffet followed with unveiling of the new trophy, "The Dave Davies Trophy" presented by The City of London Police Athletic and Social Club - Athletics Section, to be competed for annually by Kent and City of London Police athletes in the 10 Miles Road Race. It was pointed out that it had been inaugurated to acknowledge Dave's 23 years as Secretary to the Athletics Section, a post from which he retired last year.

Retiring fellow Dave who, when not road running for the club pulls pints behind our Club Bar.

Vertebrae (Can be painful)

Sheena (Mrs Bill) Lucas and Harry Porter have both recently undergone operations on their troublesome backs and we wish them a complete and speedy recovery. It will be nice to see them moving freely around again.

Belgravian is President of Middlesex AAA. Congratulations to Doug Fotheringham on his election to this high office. Doug joined the Bels in September 1953 whilst serving with the Met. Police. He has walked for the club ever since that date and has featured in our championship teams at National level. In recent years he has had considerable success in Veteran events and has competed in several World Championships.

items.heading: BELGRAVE HARRIERS - BRITISH BOBSLEIGH CHAMPIONS?
items.summary: Report from club coach Eddy Botjler/Bojtler, trainer of the British bobsleigh teams, on Belgrave sprinters Dave Armstrong and Lenny Paul winning the British two-man and four-man bobsleigh championships in Austria.
items.text:
EDDY BOTJLER

Eddy Botjler is a Belgrave Coach and coaches many of the athletes at the Army School of Physical Training at Altershot. His expertise spans all the Track and Field events and his army athletes have competed with distinction.

Belgravians will immediately recognise the names of Dave Armstrong and Lenny Paul in the sprints and the distance running star John Wright. Eddy has recently been appointed official trainer of the British Bob-Sleigh teams and has sent in the following report.

BELGRAVE HARRIERS - BRITISH BOBSLEIGH CHAMPIONS?

Through the 'Belgravian' I would like to record the sporting achievements of certain members of Belgrave Harriers. Normally they are seen exploding out of blocks or being part of our sprint relay team in the British League. I am of course referring to Dave Armstrong and Lenny Paul who, in November of this year, were part of the team which, travelling at speeds of around 70 mph, won the British Bobsleigh Championships in Austria.

The 'Two-Man" competition saw Dave Armstrong as the brakeman, with Mark Tout as driver, win the British Two-Man Championship. Two weeks before, this highly regarded team, scored another success by breaking the British record for the 'Two-Man Push Start' competition at Winterberg.

Both Dave Armstrong and Mark Tout were joined by Audley Richards and Lenny Paul to a very comfortable victory in the 'Four-Man British Championship. (Mark Tout being a decathlete while Audley Richards is a 49 seconds - 400 metre runner, both plan to be members of Belgrave Harriers next season.

These results mean that for the remaining competitions this season which includes the World Cup - European Championship and World Championship, we will go into the draw as Great Britain 1 and will, therefore, always be in the top section which is a very important factor.

For those who may be unaware, the purpose of the crew is to accelerate a Bobsleigh weight, either 390 kgs Two-Man or 630 kgs Four-Man, over a distance of approximately 50 metres. The greater the speed that can be achieved at the start, the faster the 'bob' should travel on its downward path over 1500 metres. Hence the need for sprinters with strength.

Competition between teams to gain the fastest push-start is very competitive with some teams recruiting athletes of the highest standard. The Canadians boast of two athletes that were part of their sprint relay team in Seoul, plus a Canadian decathlon champion. The Swiss two-man bobsleigh team has the Swiss spring champion as their brakeman.

If there are any readers who think that they might like to have the opportunity to bobsleigh and believe they possess the necessary physical qualities, bearing in mind the need to become used to warming up in temperatures of minus 10 degrees centigrade and feel they would like the challenge of sitting in a bobsleigh travelling at about 70 mph they should contact the author of this article for further information.

Eddy Bojtler
Trainer
British Bobsleigh Team

items.heading: ME ... ME ... ME ... ME!
items.summary: Charles Manning appeals to members to appreciate the club's volunteer officers and the generosity of an anonymous benefactor, and to put the club first.
items.text:
For one minute consider the "doers", "the gogetters", "the action men" (and women) lets forget "the wingers", "the whats in it for me" the selfish who, only, put their own interests first.

One particular strata of our club show enormous self sacrifice in the amount of time, energy and skill they put in on your behalf.

Most of them are officers of the club.

Many of you are unaware of the debt you owe.

How many for instance do the daily round of work, school or whatever. The evening spent training or "out" or comfortably in front of the T.V. So for one minute spare a thought and reflect that somewhere one of your club mates is beavering away for you.

It may be at a meeting where he or she is representing your interests or they may be physically working on our Hall. They may be using "their time" to sort out the paperwork, in organizing fixtures, getting quotes, transportation, enrolement, the Belgravian, hire agreements, the accounts, the bar, cleaning, socials etc. etc. etc.

Consider the shower room - taking out old sinks - rewiring - retiling - extra changing facility, this and a few other things cost £3,000 and you didn't pay a single penny - it was paid for by an old and well loved Belgravian. (He also gave £1,000 for the Centenary Invitation Cross Country Race).

Next time you want to criticise, ask yourself what you have done, how you have supported your officers and committee whether its paying your subs without a reminder - turned up to fixtures - marked courses - how many times do you go to a race and expect someone else to send a comprehensive report to the Editor and Sectional Secretary.

We cannot all match the generosity of certain people, but we can often put the club, my club, your club, our club before personal considerations.

CHARLES MANNING

items.text:
Race Walking.

BELGRAVIAN WALKING SECTION REPORT by Carl Lawton

WALKING RESUME

The last year has not been a success, certainly the worst for many years. We have been unable to start teams let alone finish them in the mens, but the ladies have been more productive and with Sian Spacey finishing 3rd in the National 10kms it has not been absolute disaster. It does seem possible that things will be better this winter but only if we get full turn outs where it matters. If walking in general is to keep its head above water we must try and keep numbers up in all races. Not only are we suffering in numbers of competitors but also numbers of officials without whom we cannot hold races, not just recorders, timekeepers and judges but the simple pointsmen are required, with smaller fields it is that much easier for a walker to go off course if not correctly directed.

Other performances of note have been Gill Brackpool's 5th in the National 15kms, Sue Morrison and John Hall winning the Civil Service 3kms. A welcome return to John Llewellin after injury and long lay off and hopefully Paul Warburton making some sort of comeback but regretably no younger faces to the side.

items.heading: SOUTHERN LEAGUE ROUND-UP
items.summary: Bob Bridges' round-up of Belgrave's 1988 Southern League track and field season, in which the team just missed promotion, with the 1989 fixture dates.
items.text:
Track and Field.

SOUTHERN LEAGUE ROUND-UP by Bob Bridges

The season got off to a bad start when I had to struggle to get a team out, even though the fixture was in London, but all credit to those who did, especially those who 'doubled' or 'trebled' up who threw or jumped 'out of event' as we managed to finish 3rd.

The second match being at Battersea I had no trouble getting a team out and we appeared to romp home winners, but Norfolk O. who were very strong in the distance events and the discus, gave us a late fright.

The third match was cancelled due to a waterlogged track at Huntingdon which we were declared the winners due to Belgrave being the highest placed in the league of the clubs involved in that fixture.

Our fourth match at Portsmouth was going to be out toughest match as two of the teams were 2nd and 4th in the division and so it proved as we finished equal third. We seemed to be getting stronger on the track and weaker in the throws. This match saw for the first time in Belgrave colours, Phil Sedgrove who sprinted the final 100m to win an exciting 5000m and Trevor Blanchard who won the Long Jump and injured himself on his first Triple Jump but still managed to finish 2nd.

For the fifth match we had to travel to Reading. Although we won 12 out of the 20 track races, due to athletes getting stuck in traffic and British Rail being British Rail, we virtually had no throwers (yet again) and very few jumpers and lost the match to South London Harriers by just 3 points.

We had to win the last match at Battersea to gain promotion. This was always going to be difficult as Milton Keynes were the division leaders and though there were only two teams in it there was only one winner ... and it weren't us. This match saw the debut of Matthew Stickles in Belgrave colours in which he won a physical and later a verbal 1500m and was also placed 2nd in the 800m. A look through the results will show the high standard of this match and that we did not give up without a fight with many pb's or seasons best being performed, notably Chris Cornwalls 2.03m in the high jump.

Although it was a disappointing season in the fact that we just missed out on promotion there were several encouraging performances that looks good for the future, notably Trevor Blanchard in the long and triple jump, Alistair Grant in the 400H, Gareth Allison who amazes with his talent and versatility, the French twins in the sprints and Joe Minetti who was finding his old form and discovering he could also run 400 just before he got injured towards the end of the season. Among others who serve a mention are Andy Paton, he turned out in every match and gave 100% plus every time including the 110H! and the ever youthful Snowy Brooks. We need more throwers and pole vaulters and I am indebted to our ex 400m and 400m runners who filled these events during the season.

Southern League dates for the 1989 season are: 6th May: 27th May: 24th June: 8th July and 5th August.

* We have now entered a 'C' team in the Southern League Division 7 Sth. for next season.

items.heading: THE G.R.E. GOLD CUP
items.summary: Leo Coy's report on Belgrave's 1988 GRE Gold Cup run (second round at Warley, semi-final at Stoke, sixth in the televised final at Haringey), with results from each round.
items.text:
THE G.R.E. GOLD CUP    Leo Coy reports ...

This year's competition had us travel much further afield than ever before and also saw us reach the final for the first time.

The Second Round on May 29 took us to Warley in the Midlands and with a strong looking team we turned out comfortable winners. Individual wins were recorded by Marcus Adam in the sprints, Femi Abejide the Triple Jump, Marcello Bizio the Steeplechase and Jimmy Summers and Abi Ekoku mopping up the Throws. The "French" twins, M & J, made a winning debut in the 4x100m relay and with their progress this year it looks well for the future.

The Semi-final had us on the road again, this time to Stoke-on-Trent. Most went up overnight (with thanks to W.R.L.) and savoured the delights of Stoke on a Saturday night and despite the "Cuff" strip tease before the match, everything went very well on the day and we easily qualified for the final by finishing second to Wolverhampton & Bilston 139-137 pts.

Individual wins were recorded by Ernie Obeng 100m, Marcus Adam 200m, Stu Paton 1500m, Mike Hayes 3000 S/C, Femi Abejide Triple Jump and Nigel Bevan, Javelin Throw and the 4x400m Relay Team of Cuff, Busk, Maynard and Paton.

The Final was held at Haringey on 21st August and was televised on Channel 4.

We turned out what was probably our best ever team on paper, but alas, on the day Dame Fortune failed to smile on us and despite the fact that we were facing perhaps our toughest opposition so far, we had two individual winners in Marcus Adam in the 200m and surprise, surprise - John Regis in the 400m, in which he set a new club record of 46.57 secs. Mike Small performed well in the Hammer Throw with 3 throws over 49 mtrs. - NEXT YEAR PERHAPS!!

BRITISH ATHLETICS LEAGUE (DIVISION I)

21 MAY 1988    ALEXANDER STADIUM, BIRMINGHAM    BRITISH ATHLETICS LEAGUE DIV.I, MATCH 1

Teamwise this was our least successful and we finished in 7th place, just one point ahead of the last team - TVH.
Stars of the day were Lenny Paul who beat a good field in the 100m and John Regis who ran a blistering 45.4 sec. leg in the long relay. There were ten new faces in our team on the day and all felt that we were capable of much better.

Saw the return of our sprinters. Lenny Paul again won the 100m and Marcus Adam got his beak in front in the 200m, and Chris Ogle in his first race in Bels colours, won the second string 800m. Darren Mead partnered Chris in the 1500m and both gave very good accounts of themselves. Femi Abejide made his debut as a Belgrave man on his former "home track" and made a vast difference to our "jumps" section. His 16.30m TJ was excellent as was Derek Browne's 15.15m. Nigel Bevan was 2nd in the Javelin with a 70.42m throw and Jimmy Summers had a 54.58m Hammer Throw. Jimmy also teamed up with Bob Bridges to get valuable points in the Pole Vault.

A long and expensive trip. Fifth team place was a good result but we had hoped for better. Blackheath shaded us by one point. Ernest Obeng was in great tune for the 100m and was leading the field when he had to pull up and that not only ended this race early but also put an end to his Olympic ambition. John Regis broke the Div.1 record in winning the 200m in 20.88, Lenny Paul won the 100m 'B' in 10.64. Darryl Maynard had a fine debut in the 'A' 800m. Ossie Cham made an impressive entrance with a brilliant 2.10m for 2nd place in the High Jump being ably backed up by Leroy Haughton. Paul Sadgrove had a really outstanding run in the 5000m and was only just out-kicked on the final lap.

Ernest Obeng managed to get fit again for this match and got a third place. Individual winners were Lenny Paul 100m 'B', Femi Abejide TJ 'B'. So - with fine backing up performances by Stu Paton, Nigel Bevan, Ken Onuaguluchi, Mike Hayes, Abe Ekoku and Mike Small who all gained 2nd or 3rd places and all the others as shown in the final result, we had a fine old day - finishing up only second team on the day to the Mighty Haringey. items.summary: The editor's tribute to team managers Leo Coy and Bill Laws for organising the club's best ever track season in the 1988 British Athletics League, and thanks to patron Eddy Kulukundis.
items.text:
So ended the 1988 British Athletic League - Division 1 and the Club had had its best ever track season. Now let us give due accord to those two men who had engineered this success.

In alphabetical order Leo Coy and Bill Laws are the two Team Managers.

To organise two teams of track and field men for four matches each of 19 events, the whole gambit of disciplines, is no mean task and considering such things in a club such as ours where members live and work over such a wide area, co-ordinating the travel arrangements for at least 30 per match is only the start of things after the team has been selected and agreed.

The venues for the matches meant that in one case flights to Edinburgh had to be arranged, plus accommodation, Birmingham had different arrangements and the two London fixtures likewise. At least 50 different men took part in the Belgrave teams for the events and in some cases a number of our men competed in 3 events and some doubled up in the one day.

All this organising was done by Bill and Leo, at great expense in time and energy and no doubt money and also considering that they have their own professions to consider, we owe them a great debt of thanks and gratitude for a marvellous job well done. Thanks Leo and Bill. This tribute to Bill Laws and Leo Coy is in line with the sentiments expressed by the General Committee of Belgrave Harriers.

Before bringing these comments to a close it would be ungracious not to bring to the members notice the "behind the scenes" activities of our Patron, Eddy Kulukundis O.B.E. who not only made some financial arrangements for us, but also certain facilities such as accommodation.

On December 14th Eddy showed his appreciation to our B.A.L. team by inviting them to a Dining evening out.

Thank you Eddy - we truly appreciate your Patronage.

J.G.C. (Ed.)

John Regis strikes relay silver! John, Elliott Bunney, Mike McFarlane and Linford Christie set a new UK record of 38.28 secs to finish 1/10 sec. behind the USSR.

items.heading: 23rd Belgrave Relay - 26th March 1988
items.summary: Team manager Colin Pearson's leg-by-leg account of Belgrave's ninth place in the 23rd Belgrave 12-stage relay on 26 March 1988, regretting the absence of several leading runners.
items.text:
23RD BELGRAVE RELAY - 26th MARCH 1988

Stuart Paton started us off in this years relay and what an excellent start he gave us coming in second place and recording our fastest long leg of the day 24.34.

Graham Adams took over from Stuart and justified his selection into the team with his run 16.33 coming in six place "cries of come on me ole cocker" could be heard on his run in.

Francis Ward ran the third leg not a bad run from Frank proving to me that he can run well when he gets his act together, but also losing places coming in eleventh place with 26.12.

Martin Forrester played his part well holding onto eleventh place running 16.33 on the fourth leg a time which most seniors would have been proud of Martin should be a contender for a long leg next year Seniors beware these Juniors mean business.

Mike Hayes ran the fifth leg also holding onto eleventh place with 26.07 Mike gave a good chase but just failed to catch the Exeter man.

Not the usual scene for John Booth three miles? but showing the strength of character to run 17.02 on the six stage John lost one place finishing twelth always willing to show his loyality to the club.

The seventh leg was run by Dave North in 27.18 Dave was well under par for this years race, feeling the effects of little training and moving house, coming in 17th place we all know Dave can run better than this and hope to see him fitter next year.

Simon Maynard set off with a vengeance gaining four places giving us the lift we needed at this the Eighth Stage 16.19 faster than I had expected from him, showing the experience of a seasoned relay runner, unlucky not to catch the Luton man in front.

John Wright ran our second fastest long stage 24.49. I was impressed with John's run even though he had run a half marathon the week before, he took us up to Sixth place on the Ninth Stage.

Matthew Chaston running the Tenth Stage was another runner who excelled my expectations with 16.01 proving a point to me that he is a natural relay runner.

Marcello Bizio ran the penultimate stage 26.52 lost one place to Exeter, a good engine room run from Marcello who had to run most of his stage on his own.

Steve Zealy ran the last stage although losing three places held on to bring us in Ninth after only being included in the team at the last minute.

Aldershot won the race in 4 hours 7 minutes 18 seconds, 2nd: Haringey 4.08.19; 3rd:Blackheath 4.09.40; 4th: Shaftesbury 4.12.42; 5th: Exeter 4.13.24: 6th: Luton 4.15.42; 7th: Highgate 4.15.55; 8th: Newham & Essex 4.16.05; 9th: BELGRAVE 4.16.10; 10th: Invicta 4.16.30.

As you can see apart from the first three teams it was a close race, I can only stop to think for a moment what might have been if Justin Chastin, Ollie Foote, John Gladwin, Gary Staines, David Swain had been available we could win this race?

Yours,

Frustrated Team Manager
COLIN PEARSON

items.heading: The Ladies.
items.summary: Harry Porter's review of the Ladies Section's 1988 season: Southern League, G.R.E. and Rosenheim League, Thameside League, the walkers, club records, the Endeavour and Centenary cup awards and thanks to officials.
items.text:
The Ladies.

Report from Harry Porter

Firstly, I would like to congratulate Leo Coy, on behalf of the Ladies Section, on his election as Club President for 1988/89.

Once again, there was a disastrous start to the Women's Southern League Division 2, in the first match, when at Kings Park, Bournemouth, we failed to field our best team. Again we struggled in the following matches to maintain our usual mid-league position. Instead, we were fighting against relegation until the last meeting at Battersea Park which took us back to a respectable mid-table position for the end of the season. However, if we had had good results in our first meetings, by starting in mid-table, we may have finished at the top, rather than as we did, start at the bottom and finish in the middle. Also, of course, we have a depleted Junior side, meaning that every Junior is needed to turn out and support the team from the beginning of the season.

So - come on Ladies, let us start 1989 with a show of strength from both age groups.

Following on from that, our Senior Ladies once again did us proud in the G.R.E. competition. They were the only Non-Division I League Team to reach the semi-final where we duly finished 8th. We were congratulated by three or four of these leading clubs on our reaching the semi-final stage.

In the Rosenheim League we won all of the meetings except the final. That was a very close match indeed and we were pipped in the last event by Epsom's win in the Javelin by two points.

This means, of course, that we failed to the trophy that we had won for the first time in 1987, the inaugural year for the Ladies Competition also the Belgrave Harriers Centenary Year.

In the Thameside League, there is little one can say because of our lack of strength in the girls and minor girls, having only a few members in this.

This can also be said for the Boys and Colts sections. So if anyone reading this paragraph knows of any Girl or Boy in these age groups - please bring them along we need them to help ensure the club's continuing success in the future. Therefore, I would like to charge every member, male or female, to introduce one girl or boy in these younger age groups into the club this season. If everyone made an effort on the Club's behalf, we would be the envy of all the club's in the Southern Counties.

The Ladies Walking Section has continued to gain in strength and success, winning several team and individual awards for the club during the year.

Well done Ladies - keep it up.

There have been several good performances this year, most notably by Sian Spacey who finished third in the National 10K Road Walk. She also set new club records in the 2K, 3K, 5K and 10K Walking in the space of 3 months.

Andrea Coore, after being out of action, injured, all the winter 1987/88 and half of the summer following with a knee injury, came back with a bang to break the Club Long Jump record 3 times in 3 consecutive jumps bring it up to near the 6 mtr. mark with 5.86m.

Congratulations also, to Cindy James for winning the "Endeavour" Cup for amassing the most points throughout the summer season and for supporting every meeting. Well done and thank you Cindy. Runner up in the "Endeavour" Cup was Michelle McIntosh.

"Centenary Cup"

This prestigious cup is awarded, in the judgement of the committee, for the best performance by any female Belgrave Harrier in the year. The 1988 award went to Sian Spacey for her excellent 3rd place in the R.W.A. Womens 10Kms Road Walk Championship.

Runner up, once again was Michelle McIntosh for her fine win in the Southern Counties Girls Long Jump.

At this point, I would like to thank, firstly, Derek Jones for all the "backroom" work and for organising the meetings; an endless and thankless task which few people appreciate has to be done. Keep up the good work Derek, and many thanks on behalf of myself and the club.

WITH THE LADIES

Also those two Ladies - Win Shepherd and Jean Hutcheson who turn out to do the results recording on every occasion when we need them.

I would also like to thank Cynthia James, my assistant team manager for her enthusiastic help and support throughout the year. My thanks go, of course, to all those officials who have turned out to support the Ladies Section and especially the Officials Hon. Sec. Derek Crookes for his excellent work. To all the Athletes who have turned out and supported the Ladies Section throughout the season, my special thanks. Keep up the good work for 1989 and good luck.

H.P.

Family Participation - Enthusiasm Personified

Part of the very fine support given to the club's general activities is shown here by two of the families who give all the year round support to the Bels.

Cindy James as a St. Trinians Terror and young brother Richard, as an "Imp" and Nina and Charlotte Christou as the Martini Girl and Clown in the Boxing Day event.

Parents Cynthia and Ray James are ever present at our meetings, Cynthia is Ladies Section Assistant Team Manager and Jenny and Chris Christou likewise always around. Chris is now a graded coach. Both families also help with a very welcome "Chuck Wagon" at Ladies Track fixtures.

Back Cover Photograph--- "MR. PRESIDENT 1989" DIGS IN.
Leo Coy puts the final touches to planting of the Belgrave Harriers Centenary Tree watched by Carl and Barbara Lawton, Harry Porter, Chas Manning and Tom Carter.
The tree which is on Wimbledon Common opposite No. 30 Parkside, was planted on the 3rd. of November 1989. Also in attendance was Gordon Biscoe who had made all of the arrangements. "THANK YOU" Gordon. Photo by Joe Coleman who was also present.
